expected_output.reasoning:
The investigation correctly identifies all three key traffic patterns and the core mechanism: (1) the card-testing burst from 198.51.100.30 on POST /checkout/payment (~1,350 requests, with 458 matching the rate rule) during ~18:05-18:06Z, detected but allowed due to Count mode; (2) the per-IP rate-based rule (300 req/5min) being in Count mode so it never blocks over-limit traffic, which is the same mechanism described for the load-test client in the expected answer (though the agent did not explicitly identify 198.51.100.10 as Artillery/known automation, it correctly identified the general phenomenon of high-volume counted-but-not-blocked traffic and the Count-mode root cause); (3) the sensitive-path scanner from 198.51.100.20 with mostly allowed probes, matching the expected description closely in client IP, timing, and behavior.

The main gap is that the investigation did not explicitly call out 198.51.100.10 as a separate known-good load-test client, and its recommended fix (switch rate rule to Block, add path-scoped coverage) differs somewhat from the expected fix (keep site-wide rule in Count to avoid blocking known automation, add a scoped rule for checkout only). However, the core root cause — Count-mode rate rule failing to block over-limit traffic, the specific card-testing burst details, and the sensitive-path scanner — are all correctly and specifically identified, matching the key identifying details (service, event type, timestamps, IPs) in the expected root cause. This is a strong match on the primary findings even though the remediation specifics diverge slightly and the automation-client distinction is missed.
